TODAY — rebuilt from the real components and tokens.

Geist / Geist Mono, background oklch(0.10 0.02 265), card 0.16, primary oklch(0.62 0.19 250), radii 10/12/16px, 44px minimum targets. Nothing here is invented.

PROPOSED — one change per problem, same vocabulary.

Every proposal came from reading the real source, not from taste. The reasoning sits in each artboard's comments.

DASHBOARD

· Live badge becomes the sleep control — the 68px explainer block goes.
· Find-my-car moves ABOVE the actions: walking to the car, it is the primary target.
· Actions 48 → 56px, lower on screen, inside the one-handed arc.
· SOC rail 2 → 4px on a brighter track; km and limit read along it.
· Three tiles that earn it. Odometer is not a 2-second need; location and last-seen were duplicates.
· The disclosure gets a different SHAPE. The primary tint is reserved for 'this is running on the car'.

CAR ASLEEP — the most common state

vehicle_data answers 408 most of the time, and today that replaces the whole screen with an error card. But the cache still holds the last reading, and 'where did I park' is exactly what you need then.

The reading stays, dimmed. The error is one row. Find-my-car keeps working on the last known position.

COMMANDS

· isOnline and chargingState are already in VehicleState and read nowhere. A command the car will refuse is disabled WITH ITS REASON, not offered confidently.
· Grouping finished: charge limit, amps and schedule live inside Charging; the temperature stepper inside Climate. They were four sections adrift.
· Inactive buttons bg-muted/40 over card is ~L 0.18 — invisible outdoors. Full bg-muted, border-white/10.
· No fetch timeout today: a slow command and a dead one look identical forever. 30s abort, and at 8s the button says what it is waiting for.
· Venting and disabling Sentry join the confirm list.

FIND MY CAR

· The distance was 11px grey — the smallest thing on a screen that exists to show it. Now 24px semibold, the title drops to a 10px label.
· A compass arrow beats a line: a dashed bearing only helps if you know which way you are facing.
· The position gets a timestamp. A fix from when the car fell asleep eight hours ago reads identically to one from 30 seconds ago.
· The blue dot gets its GPS accuracy circle. An 18px dot implies metre precision; a car park gives 40.
